source.title: Capability ≠ Interpretability: Human Interpretability of Vision Foundation Models
source.authors: Julien Colin; L. Goetschalckx; Nuria Oliver; Thomas Serre

record.tranche_reason: The study measures human interpretability of SAE-recovered vision features and finds that the tested foundation models score below size-matched supervised models, while interpretability is not significantly associated with downstream task performance. This challenges and qualifies parts of V4. Its novel-image localization task also bears on V6, though it uses human observers and visual features rather than automated explanations of language-model neurons.
record.gate_note: The paper tests human observers’ ability to localize and describe SAE features in vision models. It does not measure neuron-pole job counts, language-model neurons, InceptionV1 neurons, attribution graphs, or automated explanation scores. Its control experiment on ResNet-50 and ViT-B/32 tests inflation in a prior forced-choice protocol; those results are not rows because they do not measure the outcomes named by these claim versions. The paper’s model-level scores and capability correlations are included below.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It assumes the premise the essay disputes: individual vision neurons are polysemantic. It therefore swaps neurons for TopK SAE dictionary features and measures how well humans can localize and describe those features in six ViTs. No row measures neurons (or neuron poles) or a share of units with one job. None tests InceptionV1, language models, attribution graphs or automated simulation scoring. V4 concerns the share of interpretable neurons as architecture and tools improve. Here all models share the ViT architecture, differ in training objective, and are scored on SAE features by median score, not share. V6 concerns neuron explanations failing to predict firing. The localizability task is analogous but uses SAE features in vision models. These are related constructs, recorded under fits_no_version. The record's T5 / tests classification and its three labels should be dropped.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that all four foundation models tested are less interpretable than the size-matched supervised ViT-B. They find interpretability uncorrelated with downstream performance, and locality and coarse-grained human semantic alignment predict it. They also note DINOv3, whose objective promotes locality, as a partial exception suggesting the gap is not architectural destiny.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK sparse autoencoders to obtain vision features, then human psychophysics tasks for localization and description; it is not a neuron-pole job-count audit or an automated language-model explanation evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: For localizability, rescoring participant clicks with HSIC rather than RISE lowers absolute scores but preserves broad model ordering (Appendix I.1). Description plausibility rankings were also checked across alternative VLM scorers and image crops; the paper reports that the main ranking is robust.

fits_no_version.finding: Humans viewing a feature's visualization, top images and heatmaps localize SAE features on novel images above chance. Median scores are 0.71–0.86 (chance 0.5); under HSIC rescoring they are 0.58–0.74.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explanations of SAE features in vision transformers from activating examples predict where the feature fires on new images well above chance but well short of ceiling.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched ViT-B architecture and scale, SAE features of four foundation models are less interpretable than those of supervised ViT-B on localizability, plausibility and agreement (p<.001). Interpretability tracks activation locality, not capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a fixed architecture, training objective changes how interpretable a model's learned features are to humans, independent of downstream capability.

fits_no_version.finding: In the prior forced-choice protocol for neuron interpretability, participants scored above chance even with uninformative reference images. Scores were 60.0% for ResNet-50 and 53.6% for ViT-B/32. This inflates neuron interpretability scores in a model-dependent way.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human forced-choice tests of neuron interpretability overstate understanding through process-of-elimination shortcuts.

record.problems: Only six models are included and almost all are at ViT-B scale, limiting model-level statistical power. The semanticity plausibility measure uses an external VLM as a proxy for description quality. The localizability measure scores human clicks against attribution heatmaps, which are only proxy ground truth. Model comparisons do not isolate architecture or tool effects causally.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing results were left out. The forced-choice control experiment in Section 3.1 was not recorded as a row because it evaluates a prior protocol’s baseline inflation rather than the claim-version outcomes.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-count shares.
No language-model neuron shares, dense vs MoE comparison, or scale.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No share of interpretable neurons. No manipulation of architecture, regularization or tools. Neuron basis replaced by SAE features.
No attribution graphs or neuron-based circuit explanations.
No test of neuron explanations predicting activations. Localization is of SAE features, not neurons.
No automated simulation scoring of explanations.

missing.what: Forced-choice control experiment on ResNet-50 and ViT-B/32 neurons: 60.0% (CI 58.1–62.0) and 53.6% (CI 51.3–55.9) accuracy with uninformative references. It is the only neuron-basis human result in the paper and is relevant to how neuron interpretability is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The study treats neurons as polysemantic by premise and never measures neuron interpretability in its main experiment, so it cannot bear on the neuron-share claims. The record's V4 'challenges' and 'supports' labels and V6 'supports' label are removed. Model comparisons vary training objective, not architecture or tooling, and n=6 limits correlations.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or neuron-pole job-count shares.
No language-model neuron-pole shares, dense-versus-MoE comparison, or scaling to very large models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive-generalization analysis.

Does not estimate the proportion of interpretable neurons or test InceptionV1-sized vision models; does not manipulate architecture or explanation tools to establish causation. It compares six vision transformers, mostly at ViT-B scale, using SAE features and human scores. It does measure whether interpretability scores correlate with downstream performance.
No attribution graphs or neuron-based behavioral reconstruction.

Tests human localization of SAE-recovered visual features on novel images after viewing visual explanations and activating examples, not whether language-model neuron explanations predict activations on new text.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Foundation models compared with the size-matched supervised ViT-B baseline
reader_labels.reason: All four tested foundation models score below ViT-B on localizability, plausibility, and agreement (rows loc-dinov2 through agree-siglip); the paper reports the differences as significant at p < .001.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Interpretability versus downstream task performance across the six tested models
reader_labels.reason: None of the reported correlations with classification, segmentation, or perceptual grouping is statistically significant (rows perf-imagenet-loc through perf-group-agree).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Human localization of SAE visual features on novel images in the six tested models
reader_labels.reason: Scores are above chance but below the scale maximum, indicating successful yet incomplete localization after participants see the feature explanations and activating examples (rows loc-vit-s through loc-siglip). The measure is a normalized score, not a direct failure rate.
